title: Heading to Europe or the U.K. for the Aug. 12 solar eclipse? Best eclipse glasses to buy before you leave — or after you arrive
summary: We've rounded up the best solar eclipse glasses so you can watch safely from wherever you are.
contentText:
The Aug. 12 total solar eclipse is nearly here, and if you’re hoping to observe totality, you will likely be heading to Greenland, Iceland, or Spain. The UK gets a solid 90% show, while the US only catches a small partial solar eclipse.

Wherever you're watching it from, do not look directly at the sun without ISO 12312-2 certified solar eclipse glasses — standard sunglasses aren't safe and won't save your retina.

Not sure which to buy? We’ve rounded up legitimate, safe options that you can order right now from the US, UK, and European retailers, so you can stay safe and enjoy the eclipse whether you're staying put, about to travel, or already abroad.

- We've got you covered with reviews and rankings of the best telescopes , binoculars , star projectors , cameras , drones , Lego , streaming and more.

Best UK solar eclipse glasses

The difference, apart from the price, is that these have plastic frames and so should prove hardier, particularly if you're going to keep them around for the 2027 partial solar eclipse. View Deal

Get a pair of Soluna solar eclipse glasses for just £2.99, a saving of £2.00. Purchasers report that the cardboard's not the strongest but they provide proper eye protection (as always, ISO 12312-2:2015 is the standard to watch out for). View Deal

For those traveling to some parts of Europe, Greenland or western Iceland, observing the total solar eclipse in safety is important, so use a pair of solar eclipse glasses. (Image credit: Photo by Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

The 2026 total solar eclipse is coming on Aug. 12 but if you are in the USA, you won't be able to experience totality. A minor partial eclipse is visible from some states, with the best coverage in parts of Alaska and New England. You might be getting ready to travel to one of the spots that will reach totality, like Greenland, western Iceland and northern Spain. Even places in the UK will be getting their best solar eclipse since the 1999 total solar eclipse over Europe, with the moon obscuring around 90% of the sun.

If you are planning on watching it at all, you will need at the very least, a pair of solar eclipse glasses. They need to be rated ISO 12312-2 so that they block 99.999% of the sunlight and keep observation safe. Looking at the sun without proper protection can result in permanent blindness and vision problems. If you are after some sharp images of the sun, you will even need filters and solar viewing gear for your smart telescope , camera or solar binoculars .

So whether you are staying in the USA for a small but partial eclipse or travelling to Europe for a more dramatic show, we have found the best solar eclipse glasses to grab before the event. We have included retailers from America and Europe, including the best eclipse glasses in the UK. You should always check your eclipse glasses before use to make sure there are no holes or tears in them. Make sure you buy from a reputable brand and if you are unsure in any way about their eye protection ability, don't use them.
